data.name: Chinmoy
data.gender_notes: Chinmoy is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chinmoy is derived from the Sanskrit word 'chinmaya', which means 'consciousness' or 'intelligence'. This name is often used in Hinduism for boys and represents the deep inner wisdom and sensation that exists within each of us. The name Chinmoy carries the meaning “Consciousness, Intelligence, Sensation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chinmoy usually hope their child will grow to embody consciousness, intelligence, sensation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the divine consciousness within us.

historical_references.reference: Chinmoy Kumar Ghosh (1930-1993): A prominent spiritual teacher and artist of the 20th century, Chinmoy was born in Shakpur, Bengal, India. He was a disciple of the Sri Aurobindo Ashram and was known for his unique approach to spirituality, which combined elements of yoga, meditation, music, and art. Chinmoy's teachings emphasized self-transcendence and the realization of one's inner divinity.

Chinmoy Kumar Ghosh (1432-1508): A celebrated poet and philosopher of the Bengali language during the late medieval period in Bengal, India, Chinmoy is best known for his works in the genre of devotional poetry, or Bhakti poetry. His most famous work is the ‘Chaitanya Charitamrita’, a biography of the 16th-century saint Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Chinmoy's poetry reflects his deep devotion to the Hindu deity Krishna and his explorations of the spiritual path.
